Auto-generate a skeleton annotation table from a PEAKS export folder

Source: R/annotation.R
get_annot_peaks.Rd

PEAKS counterpart of get_annot_fragpipe() / get_annot_diann(): indexes the search-result subfolders of a PEAKS export with the same internal indexer read_peaks_batch() uses to pick folders, drops the QC folders, and returns one row per result folder ready to fill in.

Usage

get_annot_peaks(dir_data, drop_qc = TRUE)

Arguments

dir_data

Path to the PEAKS export root folder (the one holding the <project>_PEAKS_<nn> result subfolders).

drop_qc

Drop the _QC_ folders (default TRUE) — they are not sample results and read_peaks_batch() ignores them too.

Value

A data frame with columns Sample_folder, File_peaks_nb, Condition, BioReplicate, TechReplicate, Sample, Sample_ID, sorted by Sample_folder.

Details

One row per folder is not necessarily one row per sample. A PEAKS export folder usually holds several samples, one Area#<sample> column each inside its peptide.csv, and it is those suffixes that annotate_peaks() joins on. So for a multi-sample export, duplicate the folder's row once per sample and add a Sample_peaks column naming each sample exactly as its Area# column does; Sample_folder stays the same on every one of those rows. With one folder per sample the two keys coincide and read_annot() derives Sample_peaks for you.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
get_annot_peaks("2_data/peaks_export")
} # }
